output.reason: [ev-6e35b4906b1d] says the cluster name is now validated and the check can only be bypassed by setting `upgradeCompatibility` to v1.15 or earlier. So a non-conforming name fails validation; nothing says the name is silently not honoured, which rules out setting-ignored. `upgradeCompatibility` is the Helm attribute used to keep earlier behaviour [ev-e24450bf8fed], so the failing validation blocks the install/upgrade itself, as the proposed statement already says. That makes the kind upgrade-blocked. Confidence is low because the evidence does not name the exact component that runs the check.

correction.statement: In Cilium 1.16 a cluster name that is longer than 32 characters, uses anything other than lower case alphanumerics and '-', or does not start and end with an alphanumeric character fails the new validation. This blocks install/upgrade unless upgradeCompatibility is v1.15 or earlier. Strict enforcement starts in v1.17.

consequence.statement: The cluster name is now validated: at most 32 lower case alphanumeric characters and '-', starting and ending with an alphanumeric character. A non-conforming name fails validation, so the install/upgrade does not go through unless upgradeCompatibility is set to v1.15 or earlier. That bypass is temporary: validation will be strictly enforced starting from Cilium v1.17.
consequence.remediation: Make the cluster name conform (at most 32 characters, lower case alphanumeric and '-', starting and ending with an alphanumeric character) before upgrading. As a temporary workaround, set upgradeCompatibility to v1.15 or earlier; it stops working in v1.17.
